technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the shell (U1) as a standalone Spring Boot CLI application built on Spring Shell, communicating with the spring-cloud-data REST API through a typed client built on Spring HATEOAS and RestTemplate.
Limit shell commands for this increment to stream commands only (stream create, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list, show) per U1.

For U2, derive module metadata from @ConfigurationProperties classes using the spring-boot-configuration-processor, which generates spring-configuration-metadata.json inside each module jar; the metadata strategy component resolves and parses this metadata (including whitelisting/aliasing rules) and feeds the shell 'module info' command.

Port XD modules (U3-U8) to the spring-cloud-stream programming model: each becomes an independent Spring Boot application using @EnableBinding with Source (http, tcp, twitterstream, twittersearch) or Processor (filter, transform) interfaces, replacing XD XML module wiring with Java configuration.
Reuse Spring Integration channel adapters and transformers from the XD code base for the ported endpoints (http, tcp, twitter) rather than rewriting endpoint logic.
Baseline stack is Java 17+ with Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3, as required by the specification (Spring Framework 6 requires Java 17+).
Use the spring-cloud-stream binder abstraction (e.g., RabbitMQ or Kafka) for all module input/output channels; binder-specific code is kept out of module logic.
Structure the work as Maven multi-module builds with a shared parent pom and dependency management aligned with the spring-cloud-stream and spring-cloud-data BOMs.

Testing strategy: JUnit 5 unit tests plus Spring Boot integration tests for each ported module and for the shell; a manual end-to-end verification of composed streams against a local spring-cloud-data server.
assumptions: A single developer (the author) performs all work; estimates are personal effort in work-hours and exclude code review by others, management, and coordination overhead.
The Spring XD source code for the http, tcp, twitterstream, twittersearch, filter, and transform modules is available and can be reused as the basis for porting.
The spring-cloud-stream (s-c-s) and spring-cloud-data repositories and their core runtime already exist; this increment only adds the shell, metadata strategy, and ported modules.
U1 scope is limited to stream commands; task/job, module registry, and security commands are out of scope.
Twitter modules (U5, U6) are 'moved' with only the changes needed to adapt them to the spring-cloud-stream model; no new features are added.
CI/build infrastructure and developer workstation setup already exist; no effort is allocated to provisioning environments.
Estimates include unit tests and basic integration tests, but exclude performance, load, and security testing.
Documentation effort is limited to READMEs and reference documentation updates for the shell and the ported modules.
Third-party service access (e.g., Twitter API credentials) for testing is available.
No UI work is required; all interaction is via the shell and REST API.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the 8 user stories, study XD module code and spring-cloud-stream/spring-cloud-data APIs, and produce the overall design for the shell, the @ConfigurationProperties metadata strategy, and the module porting approach.
Set up Maven multi-module project structure, parent poms, dependency management aligned with spring-cloud-stream/spring-cloud-data BOMs, and Java 17 / Spring Boot 3 baseline for the new artifacts.
Create the Spring Boot shell application using Spring Shell, including configuration, connection handling, and a typed client over the spring-cloud-data REST API (HATEOAS traversal, RestTemplate).
Implement stream commands in the shell: stream create, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list, and show, including DSL handling, parameter parsing, and result formatting.
Write unit and integration tests for the shell application and stream commands, including mocking of the spring-cloud-data REST API.

Design and implement the metadata strategy: integrate spring-boot-configuration-processor into module builds, resolve and parse spring-configuration-metadata.json from module jars, and expose a metadata service with property whitelisting/aliasing support.
Implement the 'module info' shell command that lists all module properties using the metadata strategy, including formatting of options, types, defaults, and descriptions.
Unit and integration tests for metadata extraction, resolution, and the module info command output.

Port the XD http module to s-c-s as a @EnableBinding(Source) Spring Boot app: adapt endpoint configuration (Spring Integration HTTP inbound), define @ConfigurationProperties, generate metadata, and add unit/integration tests.
Port the XD tcp module to s-c-s as a Source app: adapt Spring Integration TCP inbound adapter configuration, serializers/deserializers options, @ConfigurationProperties, metadata, and tests.
Move the XD twitterstream module to s-c-s as a Source app: adapt to the binding model, expose credentials/options via @ConfigurationProperties, generate metadata, and add tests.
Move the XD twittersearch module to s-c-s as a Source app: adapt to the binding model, expose query/credential options via @ConfigurationProperties, generate metadata, and add tests.
Port the XD filter module to s-c-s as a @EnableBinding(Processor) app: adapt SpEL expression handling, @ConfigurationProperties, metadata, and tests.
Port the XD transform module to s-c-s as a Processor app: adapt SpEL expression handling, @ConfigurationProperties, metadata, and tests.
Run a local spring-cloud-data server and verify end-to-end streams built from the ported modules via the new shell (e.g., http | filter | transform, tcp, twitter sources), and fix integration issues.
Write READMEs and reference documentation for the shell (stream and module info commands), the metadata strategy, and each ported module's options.
Code cleanup, self-review, build verification across all modules, dependency and metadata consistency checks, and preparation of the increment for delivery.
